links.reason: 56 says only that he is no skilled dancer before the professional drummers (கோடியர் முழவின் முன்னர் ஆடல் வல்லான் அல்லன்), while 52 shows him giving the lead hand in the thunangai (துணங்கைக்குத் தழூஉப்புணை ஆகச் ... தலைக்கை தந்து); a communal dance does not contradict the denial of a performer's skill. The mock-dispraise reading is plausible from 56 alone (it turns to the battlefield dance, போர்க்களத்து ஆடும் கோவே), but the claim that it 'only works because his festival dancing was known' needs 52 to be common knowledge, which is a generous reading.

The link rests on two colophon facts: the patikam's தகடூர் எறிந்து and Purananuru 230's patron line naming Ezhini who fell at Tagadur; the poem itself names only எழினி பொருதுகளம் சேர, not Tagadur or the Chera. Victory praise and elegy for the fallen are different offices, not incompatible claims, so TENSION does not fit; the 'one poet sings both sides' point is real but depends on the tradition, not the verses.

Ainkurunuru 183 sets the evening's coming beside the backwater neythal closing (கொடுங்கழி நெய்தலும் கூம்ப), and line 6 refuses morning's relief (காலை வரினும் களைஞரோ இலரே), while Kural 1227 makes the sickness bud at காலை and bloom at மாலை. The pair gives a real flower closing against the metaphoric flower opening at the same hour, which neither verse shows alone.

The wordplay is real: Natrinai 81's wife longs to give a feast (விருந்து அயர் விருப்பொடு) and Ainkurunuru 482's man says he will come as her பெருவிருந்து. But nothing in either poem limits or conditions the other; it is a shared word turned to a new referent, which is a same_image pairing, and 'turning' suggests a development the two separate poems do not show.

Kuruntokai 42's தொடர்புந் தேயுமோ is a friend's challenge to the hero, Kainnilai 4's கலந்து உள்ளாத் தகையானோ a question about him put to the girl; both are the common doubt of the man's constancy. The 'double office' observation is fair but thin, and QUALIFIES does not describe the relation: neither limits the other.

Patikam 4 gives Narmudi Cheral the killing of Nannan and the felling of his vaakai (பொன்படு வாகை முழுமுதல் தடிந்து); Patitruppattu 88 lists சுடர்வீ வாகை நன்னன் தேய்த்து among deeds ending in பெரியோர் மருக (line 14), alongside the kadamba felled (கடம்பின் முழுமுதல் தடிந்து) and the sea-spear. The pairing shows a named king's war absorbed into the line's inherited record, which neither text shows alone.

Kuruntokai 135 quotes both halves (வினையே ஆடவர்க் குயிரே ... மனையுறை மகளிர்க் காடவர் உயிர்) and concludes அழுங்குவர் செலவே; Thinaimalai 82 argues only from ஆண்கடன்/பூண்கடன் and concludes செல்வர். The same premise yields opposite predictions about his going, a defensible tension, and the teaches sentence names exactly the half that decides it.

Both friends argue against confinement: 68 wishes for someone to say இற்செறிந்திருத்தல் அறனும் அன்றே ஆக்கமும் தேய்ம், 351 tells the mother directly that the girl has only grown paler (பசந்தனள் என்பது உணராய்) and that the millet field would restore her. The contrast of indirect and direct plea is real, but presenting two poets' poems as 'two stages' of one case is the marker's construction.

The same words இன்னே வருகுவர் stand in Mullaippattu 16 (the herd-girl to the calf, read as omen by the old women) and Nedunalvadai 155 (the foster mothers' comfort), and in both the woman will not be comforted (காணாள் கலுழ்சிறந்து; ஒல்லாள் மிகக்கலுழ்ந்து). The teaches sentence is accurate that one poem goes on to the return and the other does not, so the pair shows the same words as omen and as mere speech.

Akananuru 246 measures the gossip by the shout at Azhundur when Karikal at வெண்ணி வாயில் broke the kings and பதினொரு வேளிர், and Purananuru 66 remembers வெண்ணிப் பறந்தலை for the loser who, புறப்புண் நாணி, sat facing north. A named battle reused in an akam simile, and the note says what Paranar does with it; small slip: the loud shout is Azhundur's (அழுந்தூர் ஆர்ப்பு), not the field's.

Akananuru 195 ends on the mother's question எம்மனை முந்துறத் தருமோ? தன்மனை உய்க்குமோ?, and Ainkurunuru 399 proposes dividing the rites: நும்மனைச் சிலம்பு கழீஇ அயரினும் எம்மனை வதுவை. The pair shows the receiving house as a matter for settlement between families, which the single poems only imply.

The shared image is real and distinctive: Aimpathu 38's stag only pretends to drink the little water (சிறுநீரை ... கள்ளத்தின் ஊச்சும்) so the doe may, and Akananuru 371's bereaved stag will not drink the little water (சில்நீர் உண்ணாது). The first half of teaches holds, but the claim that 371 'bears out the friend's hope in 38' treats two poets' poems as one story, and the 371 man is still going on (போகாநின்ற), so the second claim overstates.

Thinaimalai 16's இரண்டாவது உண்டோ answers the Kural's மடலல்லது இல்லை, and the venba sets the madal in the street (மடல் மாமேல் நின்றேன் மறுகிடையே) with a single fixed demand (பூண்ஆகம்). The pairing shows the couplet's abstract 'no strength but the madal' as a public act with one condition, which the couplet alone does not.

Both are the elephant-rescue disclosure, a stock situation; 2 adds the flowers set on her hair (அள்ளி அளகத்தின் மேலாய்ந்து), 14 has the verdict தொடாஅவால் என்தோழி தோள். But 14 already contains both the rescue (கடாஅமால் யானை கடிந்தானை) and the verdict, so the claim that 2 is 'evidence' and 14 'verdict' read in order is imposed on two independent venbas.

The shared sign (Kural தொல்கவின் வாடிய தோள், பைந்தொடி சோரும்; Ainkurunuru தொன்னலம் இழந்த ... தோளே, மின்னிழை ஞெகிழ) is the common mark of separation. What the Ainkurunuru adds is the season (கார்தொடங்கின்றே, அரசுபகை தணிய), which makes it a promised-season poem; 'evidence he is overdue' is a fair but modest gain over the shared topic.

Natrinai 8's கண் போல் நெய்தல் blooms in Poraiyan's Thondi, and Akananuru 290's eyes have lost the beauty of the neythal of Kuttuvan's Thondi (தொண்டி முன்துறை ... பெருந்தண் நெய்தல் மணிஏர் மாண்நலம் ஒரீஇ). The same place-bound flower-eye pair is used in a man's first praise and a woman's grief, a meaningful shared image.

Akananuru 167 builds the ruined village hall of the road (பீர்எழு முதுபாழ் ... பொதியில்) against the bed, while Natrinai 366 argues from the north wind that rocks the sparrow's nest (குரீஇ முயன்று செய் குடம்பை ... வட புல வாடைக்குப் பிரிவோர் மடவர்) and never reaches the road. Two arguments for the same refusal is a real and specific contrast; the word உலகியல் comes from 366's colophon, not the poem.

The only connection is Parimelazhagar's Indra, which the note itself admits neither verse contains: Kural 25 names இந்திரன் but Kural 144 names no one (எனைத்துணையர் ஆயினும் ... பிறனில் புகல்). A link made entirely of commentary is not a link between the verses, and the teaches sentence says nothing the verses teach.

Akananuru 19 reproaches the heart that neither stayed (அன்றுஅவண் ஒழிந்தன்றும் இலையே) nor crosses with him (எம்மொடு இறத்தலும் செல்லாய்), while Ainkurunuru 329 says she kept it (ஒழிந்தோள் கொண்ட என் உரங்கெழு நெஞ்சே) and wonders if it will return. Wavering versus taken is a real difference in the account of the divided heart.

Both Paranar poems use Nannan as a scale of cruelty: Kuruntokai 292 the girl killed for the fruit (பெண்கொலை புரிந்த நன்னன் போல), Natrinai 270 நன்னன் கூந்தல் முரற்சியின் கொடிதே, turned on a mother and on a husband. The teaches sentence's 'one king's notorious offence' should be 'offences', since the hair-cutting is a different deed, and 270's sense is uncertain.

The same poet answers the blazon twice: Kalittokai 14 lists the praised parts and says இனி அறிந்தேன் அது துனி ஆகுதலே, and 22 answers each praise with the aged part (பல்லின் பறி முறை பாராட்டினையோ, தளர்முலை). Past praise withdrawn and praise never extended to old age together make the blazon a whole-life claim.

Kalittokai 139 swims the sea of love with the madal as raft (மா மேலேன் என்று மடல் புணையா நீந்துவேன் ... காமக் கடல்), and Kural 1134 has the flood of love carry off the raft of நாணொடு நல்லாண்மை. The pairing turns on a shared and distinctive figure: the raft lost to the flood is replaced by the very act of shamelessness, which neither verse says alone.

Kalittokai 62 line 7 states the rule almost in the Kural's terms (தமக்கு இனிது என்று வலிதின் பிறர்க்கு இன்னா செய்வது நன்று ஆமோ), and the reply argues from the drinker's need (வேட்டார்க்கு இனிது ஆயின் அல்லது ... நீர் உண்பவர்) and holds seizing to be அறன். A real staged contest of the maxim; the attribution of lines 14-15 to the man is the marker's reading of an uncertain passage.

Kural 1150 welcomes the gossip (யாம்வேண்டும் கெளவை), Natrinai 72 fears the man's new anxiety about it (அலர் வந்தன்றுகொல் என்னும் ... புலர்வதுகொல் அவன் நட்பு). These are different situations rather than incompatible claims, and the Kural's speaker and overhearing man come from Parimelazhagar, not the couplet. Read as a condition on when gossip helps, it is a qualification.

Akananuru 38 ends with the friend's regret 'அவ்வெள் அருவிசூடிய உயர்வரைக் கூஉம் கணஃது எம்ஊர்' எனத் ... அறிவுறல் மறந்திசின், and Aimpathu 12 is that telling: காவல் இயற்கை ஒழிந்தேம், தூஅருவி ... பாக்கம் இதுஎம் இடம். Same end of guarding, same waterfall-marked village, so the pair shows the pointing out of the home as the friend's move at harvest.

Naladiyar 45 sets the jasmine-bud teeth (முல்லை முகைமுறுவல்) against the teeth fallen in the burning ground to refuse desire, while Kalittokai 22 answers the praise of முல்லை நேர் முகை teeth with பல்லின் பறி முறை to bind him to her whole life. Same compliment, same decay, opposite conclusions about staying with a woman: a defensible tension.

The phrase is shared exactly: Natrinai 167 துறைவன் தூதொடும் வந்த ... பாண நின் வாய்ப் பணி மொழி, Kainnilai 51 சேர்ப்பற்குத் தூதொடு வந்த பணிமொழிப் புள்ளே பற. The venba gives the refused envoy's formula to a bird told to fly off, a specific transfer; line 2's lacuna leaves the man's deed unclear.
links.text_issue: Kainnilai 51 line 2 is partly lost (dots in the source).

links.reason: Both are Kayamanar's mothers after an elopement; 189's foster mother widens the loss to the town (ஊர்இழந் தன்று தன் வீழ்வுஉறு பொருளே) and 195's mother asks which house will receive the girl. The contrast is real, but 189 also has her own bewildered grief at home (மனைமருண்டு இருந்த என்), so 'public versus practical' simplifies, and the shared situation does most of the work.

Verbal echo is close: Kural வாளற்றுப் புற்கென்ற கண்ணும் ... நாளொற்றித் தேய்ந்த விரல், Thinaimalai 99 வாள்இழந்த கண் ... மெல்விரலும் நாள்இழந்த எண்மிக்கு நைந்து. The venba frames the two proofs as an answer to the friend's வாளா (line 2), so the lament becomes a retort, which the couplet does not show.

The shared word is அணங்கு: Natrinai 155's man asks அணங்கோ of the girl, Ainkurunuru 182's friend says the one who struck her is கடவுள் அல்லன். But in 155 the girl is the possible goddess and the 'cure' is her smile and tears, not the naming of a human striker, so the teaches sentence's 'in both the cure ... the striker turns out to be a human lover' is false for 155.

Both refuse a straying husband, the commonest marutham situation. The Kural's reason is that all women feast on him with their eyes (கண்ணின் பொதுஉண்பர்), the Akananuru's is a reported marriage (வதுவை அயர்ந்தனை என்ப) and its refusal a mocking release (சென்றீ ... நிற் றகைக்குநர் யாரோ); calling the couplet the 'end point' of the scene restates the shared topic and asserts a derivation neither verse shows.

The echo is real: Kural 1151 வல்வரவு வாழ்வார்க் குரை and Natrinai 19 வருவை ஆகிய சில் நாள் வாழாளாதல் நற்கு அறிந்தனை சென்மே. But the claim that it works 'inside a friend's demand for marriage in the secret stage' comes from the colophon (வரைவு கடாயது); the poem itself names no marriage, so the kalavu use rests on tradition about the poem.

Both report the mother's ban: Akananuru 20 அன்னை கடிகொண் டனளே, Kainnilai 52 அன்னையும் இல்கடிந்தாள். The overhearing in 20 is the colophon's (சிறைப்புறத்தானாக), and Kainnilai 52's 'உரையேனோ பட்ட பழி' is a question whether to tell, not a message; the difference in mode is thin over a shared situation.

Purananuru 185's cart of protection (காவற் சாகாடு) running well only with a skilled driver is a general maxim, and Perumpanarruppadai 443-446 praises justice and gifts (முறைவேண்டுநர்க்கும் குறைவேண்டுநர்க்கும்) with no cart, mire or enmity. The identity of the king rests on both colophons, and 'answers the king's worry' assigns an intention the poem does not show.

Paripadal 10.65-68 shows lovers hiding their joy for fear of talk (அலர் அஞ்சி ... கரப்பார்), and Akananuru 266 charges the husband with bathing நாண்இழந்து. The contrast is real, but the Paripadal passage is hard and the Akananuru's point falls on the broken oath (சேஎயொடு உற்ற சூளே), not the shame, so the reading needs generosity.

The nature-theatre is distinctive and shared: Akananuru 82 has bamboo as flute, waterfall as drum and வண்டுயாழ் with the peacock as dancer, Thinaimalai 111 has கானம் கடியரங்கா, கோடல் hands, வண்டு யாழாக and the peacock dancing. Moving the device from kurinji disclosure to mullai waiting (உளராகி உய்யும் வகை) is a real change of occasion.

Kural 1183's exchange (சாயலும் நாணும் அவர்கொண்டார் ... நோயும் பசலையும் தந்து) becomes in Thinaimozhi 36 the friend's charge தந்தாயும் நீயே ... கொண்டாயும் நீ, with நொந்தால் உன்னைச் செயப்படுவது என் உண்டாம். The same giving and taking is turned from lament to accusation, which the pair shows and neither alone.

The signs differ: the Kural's sneeze is aborted (தும்மல் சினைப்பது போன்று கெடும்) and the venba's sneezes repeat (அடுத்தடுத்து ஒள்ளிய தும்மல் வரும்), so the same belief gives different verdicts on different evidence, which is not a tension. The teaches sentence about one folk belief serving doubt and hope is true; the pairing is a shared image.

Both open the thonri like a lamp in the rains (Akananuru 235 தோன்றி சுடர்கொள் அகலின்; Kar Narpathu 26 கார்த்திகை ... விளக்கிற் ... தோன்றி), and the heroine reads it as his forgetting (மறந்தனர் கொல்லோ) while the friend reads the rain as தூதொடு வந்த மழை. One sign read against and for him by different speakers is a defensible tension and specific.

Ainkurunuru 355 turns back without blessing the wealth-quest (சொல்லாது பெயர்தந்தேனே), Akananuru 337 remembers a heart that said அவணதாகப் பொருள் and is now tempted again. That the return is reopened is already in 337 alone; calling 337 'the sequel the decade leaves out' joins two poets' poems into one story.

The same image of the shore as a royal army is given two tempos: 52 வேந்து கிளர்ந்தன்ன ... விரையாது with நாள் ஆய்ந்து வரைதல் அறம், 53 தேறாத மன்கிளர்ந்த போலும் with எமர் முன்கிளர்ந்து எய்தல் முடி. The teaches sentence is accurate: the image sets the pace of the plea.

The exact phrase is shared: Akananuru 26 சிறுபுறம் கவையினனாக after he says 'யாமும் காதலம் அவற்கு', and Ainkurunuru 404 தானவன் சிறுபுறம் கவையினன் நன்று while she nurses. Knowing the gesture ends a sulk in 26 gives the sevili's நன்று in 404 a sharper sense.

Kural 1227 grades the sickness through the day to its bloom at மாலை, while Kuruntokai 234 overturns the definition (மாலை என்மனார் மயங்கியோரே) and makes dawn and day evening too (பெரும்புலர் விடியலு மாலை பகலும் மாலை துணையிலோர்க்கே). The Kural allows a lighter morning that the Kuruntokai denies, a real disagreement on one reading.

poems.note: The kaanthal is joined to women's fingers by போல, and line 6 states the moral (நன்றி விளைவும் தீதொடு வரும்) itself.
Lines 3 and 4 are obscure; the kingfisher's waiting cannot be given a sense for the lovers.
அதுவே சாலும் states the contentment the kuravu scene might imply.
The koels' call is stated as the cause of her weeping (கேட்டொறும் கலுழும்), a sound rather than an act.
Lines 3 and 4 repeat (சென்றனர் நம்மே); the fire of line 5 is an open simile (தீயின்).
The reed touching the neighbouring mango could point to straying, but the poem only praises his chest and no thurai names the situation.
A catalogue of flowers; no device.

iraicchi.act: sleeps alone in the ngaazhal grove of his shore
iraicchi.sense: even a lone heron sleeps in peace on his shore while she, left alone by him, cannot and pales

iraicchi.act: the herd with its calves comes home at evening
iraicchi.sense: even the cattle return to their young at evening, but he has not returned in the promised season

poems.note: Turns on கலை as the langur; the late netting after the fruit is touched maps to the guarding that follows the affair.
The elephant's shame after wrecking the vengai fits no clear part of the love situation.
The lizard's call is an omen, a sound, not an act.

iraicchi.act: the waterfall roars and gives water even when the clouds have not rained for many days
iraicchi.sense: his hill gives without being asked while he, its lord, fails her, which is why she says சான்றோய் அல்லை

poems.note: The neythal is joined to the bathing women's eyes by மானும, and only her hiding matches the submerged flower.
The tree on the strong bank is an open simile (போல).
Most of the verse is lost (dots in the source); nothing can be tagged.
அன்ன in line 2 may join the bee to the man of the town, which would make it an open comparison.
The Thirumavunni story is a legend, not a native thing of the poem.
